title: Rethinking Expressivity and Efficiency in Test-Time Training
claim: A recurrent fast-weight memory is updated at each token from key-value pairs and then read out by the query.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right recurrence, dashed box around one time step
description: A single rounded-rectangle panel with a light gray background. Row labels sit on the left: "Output tokens" at the top, "Fast weights" in the middle, and "Input tokens" at the bottom. In the middle row, an arrow carries W_{t-1} into a white rounded box labeled "Update". Another arrow goes from the box to W_t, and a further arrow runs from W_t to an ellipsis, which shows the recurrence continuing. A dashed rounded rectangle encloses one time step. Below the Update box, arrows from k_t and v_t point up into it, and an arrow from q_t points up into W_t. A curly brace splits the input x_t into k_t, v_t and q_t. An arrow runs upward from W_t to the output o_t. The figure is black and white, and the eye goes first to the central Update box.
caption: Token-wise TTT. At each step, the pair $(\boldsymbol{k}_t,\boldsymbol{v}_t)$ defines a self-supervised loss whose gradient step (the "training" stage) updates $W_{t-1}$ to $W_t$. The query $\boldsymbol{q}_t$ then reads from $W_t$ to produce $\boldsymbol{o}_t$.
abstract: Test-Time Training (TTT) enables long-context processing via continuous weight updates during inference, but current methods struggle to balance the hardware efficiency of chunk-wise approximations with the expressivity of per-token update dynamics such as learning rate and momentum. We propose E$^2$-TTT (Expressive and Efficient TTT) to bridge this gap. Following prior chunk-wise TTT methods, we compute all gradients within a chunk at the chunk-start weights. Under this setting, we derive a closed-form chunk update that retains these per-token dynamics and exactly reproduces the chunk-end state of the corresponding token-wise recurrence. This enables fully parallelized chunk-level training while preserving the temporal structure of the update rule that prior chunk-wise methods discard. We validate E$^2$-TTT by training models up to 1.3B parameters from scratch. It performs on par with previous TTT and hybrid attention baselines in language modeling while outperforming them on in-context retrieval. Its advantage is most pronounced in length extrapolation: on the standard "Needle in a Haystack" passkey test, it retains over 90% accuracy at $8\times$ the training context length. Meanwhile, E$^2$-TTT can match the training throughput of efficient chunk-wise methods, demonstrating that it effectively reconciles expressivity with efficiency. The code is available at https://github.com/zeyun-zhong/E2-TTT.
